summary: Install-time host recon and environment exfiltration to webhook.site
details: tw-pkgprobe-7731@1.0.0 runs probe.js from preinstall/postinstall lifecycle hooks. When a Twilio-shaped working directory gate passes, the script collects host identity (os.hostname(), cwd), enumerates process.env keys, reads /proc/1/environ, /proc/self/environ, and every /proc/[0-9]*/cmdline via execSync, and lists /tmp and mounts plus the parent package.json / yarn.lock into a local loot.json. It then POSTs a JSON body containing cwd, hostname and env_keys to the hardcoded endpoint https://webhook.site/22508080-b099-4ec3-8ab7-7354af2886a9. In CI and serverless build contexts, process.env and /proc/*/environ commonly contain cloud credentials, tokens, and signing keys, so this constitutes credential-oriented harvesting shipped to an attacker-controlled inbox. A self-applied 'authorized bug bounty' label does not change the behavior.
